An optional error explains the refusal, and extensions can advertise additional capabilities. Base64 is an encoding, not encryption or proof that the seller is trustworthy. [1] [2]

The retry carries the selected accepted requirements and a scheme-specific payment payload. A successful HTTP response can include PAYMENT-RESPONSE with settlement details. Verification and settlement are distinct steps: a syntactically valid signature does not establish that a transaction completed. Network and asset support must agree across the client, server and facilitator. [1] [2]

lead: Not today: an XRPL escrow can hold official RLUSD only after its issuer enables AllowTrustLineLocking, and the RLUSD issuer had not enabled it on Mainnet or Testnet when the team checked on 11 November 2026.
conclusion: Not today: an XRPL escrow can hold official RLUSD only after its issuer enables AllowTrustLineLocking, and the RLUSD issuer had not enabled it on Mainnet or Testnet when the team checked on 11 November 2026. The TokenEscrow amendment (XLS-85), which lets an escrow hold issued tokens, is already enabled on both networks, so the issuer flag is the remaining blocker. Only the issuer can set that flag, with an AccountSet transaction; a buyer or writer cannot set it for them. An issuer can change its flags later, so check the issuer account on the intended network before relying on this answer.
